title: Roasted Hazelnut Chocolate Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Chocolate custard set with a little cornflour, made with demerara sugar and finished with dark-roasted crushed hazelnuts instead of vanilla.
summary: A chocolate version of our classic custard, set with a little cornflour and made with demerara sugar, then studded with dark-roasted crushed hazelnuts. Deep, nutty and rich.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Roast the nuts
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Roast the hazelnuts on the tray for about 10 min until deep golden, then rub off the skins in the tea towel. Cool and crush coarsely with the rolling pin.

steps.title: Make the chocolate base
steps.text: Warm the milk, cream and sugar, whisking, without letting it boil. Whisk in the cocoa until smooth, then the chocolate until melted.

steps.title: Prepare the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks, salt and cornflour together in the heatproof bowl until smooth.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisk about 250 ml of the hot chocolate mixture into the yolks, then pour everything back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir constantly over low heat for about 5 min, until the custard reaches 77-80 °C and has thickened slightly.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Strain, cool in the iced water and chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and add nuts
steps.text: Churn until semi-firm, stir in the hazelnuts and freeze for at least 4 h, or overnight.

tips: Roast the nuts until really dark; pale hazelnuts taste of little.
A common mistake is letting the chocolate base boil, which can make it grainy.
The custard can be made a day ahead and kept in the fridge.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
